briefdescription.para: Demonstrates the GPIO PS driver (XGpioPs) in interrupt-driven mode.

detaileddescription.para: This file contains a design example that uses the GPIO driver (XGpioPs) in an interrupt driven mode of operation.
The example uses the interrupt capability of the GPIO to detect push button events and set the output LEDs based on the input.

simplesect.para: This example assumes that the hardware design contains a UART device. This example supports only the zcu102 board on the ZynqMP platform and only the zc702 board on the Zynq platform. For the ZynqMP platform, the input pin is 22 (sw19 on the zcu102 board) and the output pin is 23 (DS50 on the zcu102 board). For the Zynq platform, the input pins are 12 (sw14 on the zc702 board) and 14 (sw13 on the zc702 board), and the output pin is 10 (DS23 on the zc702 board). SW15 on the zc702 board is a combination of sw13 and sw14. To operate either of the input pins, keep SW15 low (both should be 00). This example supports the VCK190 and VMK180 for Versal, but requires a PL shim. See Answer Record AR# 75677 and Figure 61 in AM011 Versal TRM for more details. The driver supports both PS GPIO and PMC GPIO. To access PMC GPIOs, set "GPIO.PmcGpio = 1" in the application. Otherwise, the application accesses PS GPIO.
